title: 228 Indians flown home from Mae Sot after Myanmar scam-centre rescue
detail: Indian mission in Thailand said 228 Indian nationals rescued from scam centres in Myanmar were repatriated from Mae Sot on a special Indian Air Force flight.
attribution: Embassy of India in Thailand via IANS

title: Three Chinese who fled Myanmar scam crackdown arrested in Bangkok
detail: Police said three Chinese nationals who had entered Thailand via a natural crossing in Mae Sot after fleeing Myanmar were found in a rented room in Bangkok preparing to travel onward; they had overstayed by more than 360 days.

title: Thai army shows seized O'Smach scam base with fake police stations
detail: Thai military said the O'Smach complex it seized in Cambodia's Oddar Meanchey province held thousands of people and contained 871 SIM cards, dozens of phones, scam scripts and mock police offices imitating Brazil, China and Australia; Cambodia's interior ministry disputed the characterisation.
attribution: Royal Thai Army; disputed by Cambodian Interior Ministry

title: Chiang Rai governor warns of scam networks in Tachileik and Kings Romans zone
detail: Chiang Rai officials cited 771 suspects arrested in a crackdown in the Kings Romans (Golden Triangle) SEZ in Laos and 288 foreign workers arrested for related offences between Oct 2025 and Jan 2026, and warned residents against cross-border job offers and renting out bank accounts.

title: Kings Romans / Golden Triangle SEZ
detail: Chiang Rai officials described the Kings Romans zone in Laos as a scammer hideout, citing 771 suspects arrested in a recent crackdown there.

title: Tachileik call-centre hub
detail: Chiang Rai officials identified Tachileik, opposite Mae Sai, as a major call-centre hub.

title: Cambodia says 190 scam sites sealed, ~11,000 workers deported
detail: Cambodia's anti-scam commission head said 190 locations had been sealed, 173 people arrested and about 11,000 workers deported, citing a Kampot complex with scripts targeting Thai victims and a fake Indian police station.
attribution: Cambodia Commission for Combating Online Scams (Chhay Sinarith)

title: Mitta Lin Myaing: new scam buildings south of Myawaddy
detail: The Irrawaddy reported at least seven new buildings under construction at Mitta Lin Myaing, about 8 km south of Myawaddy, in an area controlled by Karen BGF Brigade 4, citing residents who said scam-related construction traffic was constant.

title: 'KK Park 2.0' (Qingsong Park / Thai Hoa Garden) near former KK Park
detail: The Irrawaddy reported a site called Qingsong Park or Thai Hoa Garden, about 5 km from the demolished KK Park, with satellite imagery showing 44 structures; workers reportedly call it 'KK Park 2.0'.
attribution: Workers and satellite imagery via The Irrawaddy

title: Illegal cross-border internet relay dismantled in Mae Sot
detail: True Corporation, the police Anti-Online Scam Centre and NBTC dismantled an illegal relay in Mae Tao subdistrict that was transmitting internet signals across the Moei River into Myanmar, after abnormal traffic was detected on 22-25 February.
attribution: True Corporation / Royal Thai Police ACSC / NBTC

title: UK sanctions operator of Cambodia's '#8 Park' and Xinbi marketplace
detail: The UK sanctioned Legend Innovation, described as operator of '#8 Park' (reported capacity for 20,000 trafficked workers), the Xinbi crypto marketplace, three individuals and several London properties.
attribution: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

title: Thailand opens seized O'Smach 'scam city' to media and rights groups
detail: The Joint Information Centre on the Thai-Cambodian situation led a media inspection of the O'Smach complex, alleging detention rooms, medical facilities and scam workstations, and offered to host international organisations such as Amnesty International.
attribution: Thai Joint Information Centre (ACM Prapas Sonjaidee)

title: O'Smach Resort compound (Thai-held)
detail: AP reported the 80-hectare O'Smach Resort had 157 buildings, 29 used for scam operations, and an estimated 10,000 workers per the Thai military; it is owned by US-sanctioned Cambodian tycoon Ly Yong Phat and was seized by Thai forces in December 2025.

title: US sanctions Cambodian senator Kok An and 28 others over scam network
detail: OFAC designated Senator Kok An, his Crown Resorts and 28 other persons and entities, saying casinos and resorts in Poipet, Sihanoukville and Bavet were converted into scam compounds; Heng Feng Cambodia Bank was among those designated.

title: US offers $10m reward over DKBA-protected Tai Chang scam estate
detail: The Irrawaddy reported the US State Department offered up to $10 million for information leading to seizure of Tai Chang scam estate proceeds in Kyauk Khet, and that US prosecutors charged two Chinese nationals over the Shunda Park compound in Min Let Pan.
attribution: US State Department / US Justice Department

title: Tai Chang scam estate, Kyauk Khet (DKBA area)
detail: Named by US authorities as a scam estate in Kyauk Khet operating under DKBA protection; The Irrawaddy later reported operations moving from Kyauk Khet to DKBA headquarters at Sone See Myaing.
attribution: US State Department via The Irrawaddy

title: Shunda Park, Min Let Pan
detail: US prosecutors named Shunda Park in Min Let Pan village, Karen State, as a scam compound; it was reported seized by anti-regime forces in November 2025.
attribution: US Justice Department via The Irrawaddy

title: Myanmar military raids remote scam compound in Mong Pan
detail: Shan Herald reported military authorities arrested 52 Chinese and 4 Myanmar nationals at a remote compound about 20 miles north of Mong Pan town, seizing computers and Starlink units; further arrests were reported in Tachileik (27 Apr) and Muse (29 Apr).

title: Scam operations resume in Shwe Kokko in rented houses and hotels
detail: The Irrawaddy reported syndicates restarted in Shwe Kokko from late February, dispersing into rented houses, guesthouses and hotels under the Karen National Army (ex-BGF), with Chinese the majority of workers and growing numbers of Pakistani, Indian and Myanmar nationals.

title: Thmor Da casino scam base (Thai-held)
detail: The Nation reported Thai forces had taken control of the Thmor Da casino area opposite Trat as one of several border scam bases collectively valued at about 10 billion baht.

title: Chong An Ma scam base (Thai-held)
detail: The Nation listed the Chong An Ma area on the Ubon Ratchathani frontier among scam bases Thai forces said they had captured and would hold 'for as long as it takes'.

title: Thailand says it will hold captured border scam bases indefinitely
detail: Thai military said it controls scam bases at O'Smach (over 160 buildings in zones A-G), Thmor Da, Chong An Ma and casino areas opposite Sa Kaeo, worth about 10 billion baht, and will keep control to stop networks returning.
prov: Surin / Trat / Ubon Ratchathani / Sa Kaeo

title: Cambodia deports 635 Thais after Poipet 13-storey building raid
detail: Cambodian authorities raided 'Building F', a 13-storey building about 3 km from the border in Poipet, and returned 635 Thais via Ban Khlong Luek checkpoint; Thai screening found 68 complaint case IDs linked to some returnees and about 580 were allowed home.

title: Poipet 'Building F' scam and gambling building
detail: The Nation described a 13-storey building ('Building F') in Poipet about 3 km from the Thai border raided by Cambodian authorities for suspected scam and online gambling operations.

title: Three Poipet returnees arrested on outstanding warrants
detail: Sa Kaeo police said warrant checks on the 635 repatriated Thais led to the arrest of three people wanted for offences including murder, embezzlement and illegal online gambling/money laundering.

title: 18 Thais returning from Cambodia held over mule-account links
detail: Chanthaburi police detained 18 Thais at Ban Phak Kad crossing after they completed Cambodian prison sentences; seven were listed as linked to scam mule accounts in over 60 fraud cases and four had warrants.

title: 16 people fleeing Poipet scam compound caught at border
detail: Burapha Task Force and ranger units intercepted 16 people crossing via natural routes: 4 Thais (recruited to an online gambling site in Poipet), 2 Vietnamese and 10 Shan migrants from Myanmar.
place: Ban Phu Nam Kliang, Pa Rai

title: Yong Nee Oo Resort scam hub (UWSA area)
detail: A Shan Human Rights Foundation report described Yong Nee Oo Resort as a UWSA-controlled scam hub, with survivors allegedly moved to a rare-earth mine near Mong Sat less than 8 km from the Thai border.

title: KK Park (largely demolished)
detail: The Irrawaddy cited regime claims that 635 buildings were demolished and 2,000 arrested at KK Park, while only 3 of 77 marked buildings in Shwe Kokko had been razed over five months.
attribution: Myanmar regime claims via The Irrawaddy

title: Junta resumes demolishing Shwe Kokko and KK Park buildings
detail: Thai officials in Mae Sot reported two backhoes demolishing scam-linked buildings in Shwe Kokko and KK Park at about two buildings a day; analysts said earlier demolitions were largely performative.
attribution: Thai officials in Mae Sot; GI-TOC analyst

title: Junta marks 77 Shwe Kokko buildings for demolition
detail: Karen News reported the junta, with BGF/KNA cooperation, inspected over 300 illegal structures, identified 77 buildings running scams and had 74 left to demolish as of 25 May; critics called it symbolic.
attribution: Myanmar junta state media; KIC source

title: Recruiter who lured Thais to Tbong Khmum compound arrested
detail: The police Anti-Trafficking in Persons Division, using data shared by Meta, arrested an alleged ringleader in eastern Thailand accused of luring Thais to a scam compound in Tbong Khmum, Cambodia; at least five victims filed complaints.

title: Thailand reports 24bn baht seized in nine-month scam crackdown
detail: The Nation reported authorities seized over 24 billion baht in assets, closed 351,884 mule accounts and arrested 29,233 suspects, listing dismantled border scam bases including O'Smach, Thmor Da, Poipet, KK Park, Shwe Kokko, Minletpan, Tachileik and Bokeo.

title: OFAC expands Prince Group sanctions, hits Thailand-based hotel firm
detail: Treasury designated 9 individuals and 26 entities tied to the Cambodia-based Prince Group TCO, including Thailand-based White Horse Hotel Management Group Co., Ltd.

title: Rights group says 5,300+ still held in DKBA-area scam centres
detail: Thai-based CSNHTV told Thai police more than 5,300 people, including about 1,600 Chinese and 200 Myanmar nationals, remain in four locations in DKBA-controlled areas near the Thai border.
attribution: Civil Society Network for Human Trafficking Victim Assistance (CSNHTV)

title: Laos deports 24 Thais suspected of scam work via Chiang Khong bridge
detail: 24 Thai nationals (15 men, 9 women) suspected of working for call-centre scam networks were handed over at the 4th Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge; two had outstanding warrants and Thai cyber police opened an investigation.

title: 11 people fleeing Poipet jobs arrested crossing into Sa Kaeo
detail: Burapha Task Force soldiers arrested 7 Bangladeshis, 2 Vietnamese, 1 Chinese and 1 Thai who said they fled unpaid work in Poipet and paid smugglers 8,000 baht each to cross.
place: Ban Ang Sila, Non Mak Mun

title: Junta claims 69 Shwe Kokko scam buildings demolished
detail: The junta said it demolished 69 scam buildings in Shwe Kokko; residents quoted by Mon News called it political theatre and said operations continue at Shwe Kokko, Phalu, Kyaukhtat and near Ma Htaw Thalay.
attribution: Myanmar junta; residents via Mon News

title: 'AA' complex near Ma Htaw Thalay
detail: BNI/Mon News residents named a complex called 'AA' near Ma Htaw Thalay as still active in Myawaddy Township.

title: Phalu scam sites (DKBA security)
detail: Residents said scam operations remain active at Phalu border gate, where the DKBA provides security.

title: Laos raids Vientiane scam base, 589 held including 373 Thais
detail: Lao Ministry of Public Security's special anti-scam unit raided a building in Ban Dong Phosi, Hadxaifong, detaining 589 people: 373 Thai, 199 Lao, 15 Vietnamese and 2 Cambodian.

title: EU sanctions DKBA, Prince Group and Jin Bei Group over scam centres
detail: The Council of the EU listed seven persons and three entities, including the DKBA (Karen State near Myawaddy), Prince Holding Group and chairman Chen Zhi, and Jin Bei Group and chairman Zhu Zhongbiao, with asset freezes and travel bans.

title: Cambodia claims scam compounds eradicated; experts sceptical
detail: Cambodia's anti-scam commission said 624 of 793 suspected sites were raided, about 30,000 detained and 58,266 foreigners deported; Amnesty International and an anti-trafficking consultant were sceptical. Al Jazeera named O'Smach Casino at the Chong Chom crossing.

title: Myanmar Witness says Shwe Kokko demolition claims were faked
detail: Myanmar Witness analysis of the regime's claimed 25 May-26 July demolition of 77 of 322 structures found mislocated sites, AI-generated imagery and exaggerated building heights.

title: OFAC sanctions Xinbi Guarantee marketplace
detail: Treasury designated Xinbi Guarantee, Singapore-based SafeW Technology and Cambodia-based Anwen Technology, saying the marketplace processed over $24 billion mainly in Southeast Asia.

title: Sone See Myaing (DKBA HQ) scam relocation
detail: The Irrawaddy reported Chinese-run scam operations relocating from Kyauk Khet to the DKBA headquarters at Sone See Myaing, citing residents and Telegram job ads.

title: Shwe Kokko: at least 18 new scam sites
detail: The Irrawaddy said at least 18 new sites were identified in Shwe Kokko by early September, and listed active operations at Thitkate village, Hpakalu, Payathonzu, Sone See Myaing, Hpalu and Myawaddy.

title: Payathonzu (Three Pagodas Pass) scam activity
detail: The Irrawaddy listed Hpaya Thonezu (Payathonzu), opposite Sangkhla Buri, among Karen State locations with active scam operations.
